title: AppTest: an `st.components.v2` component defined in an imported module is "not registered" in later AppTest instances
body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary An app that imports an inline `st.components.v2.component(...)` from another module works under `streamlit run`, but in a test suite only the first `AppTest` that imports that module can render it: every later `AppTest` in the same Python process records `StreamlitAPIException: Component '' is not registered.` in `at.exception`. If anything imports the module before the first `AppTest` runs (a `conftest.py`, another test), that one fails too, so results depend on test order. A component defined in the script body itself is not affected, because it registers again on every run. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python # my_component.py import streamlit as st greeting = st.components.v2.component("greeting", html="

hi

") # app.py from my_component import greeting greeting(key="g") # test_app.py from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest def test_first_apptest_renders_the_component(): at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run() assert not at.exception, at.exception[0].value def test_second_apptest_renders_the_same_component(): at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run() assert not at.exception, at.exception[0].value ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Put the three files in one directory. 2. Run `pytest test_app.py`. ### Expected Behavior Both tests pass, the same way `streamlit run app.py` renders the component every time. ### Current Behavior ``` E AssertionError: Component 'greeting' is not registered. 1 failed, 1 passed ``` The first test passes and the second fails. Each test passes when run on its own. If `import my_component` is added at the top of `test_app.py`, both fail. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0) - Python version: 3.14.7 - Operating System: macOS 27.0 - Browser: n/a (AppTest) ### Additional Information **Why it happens.** `st.components.v2.component()` registers the definition once, when it is called (normally at module import), into `get_bidi_component_manager()`. That is the active runtime's registry, or a throwaway local `BidiComponentManager` when no runtime exists. `AppTest` creates one `BidiComponentManager` per instance (reused across that instance's reruns) and only runs `discover_and_register_components()` on it, which scans installed component packages. Python caches the module, so later instances never re-run the `component()` call, and the name is missing from their registry. **Workaround.** Make the module re-import inside each test's run: ```python # conftest.py import sys import pytest [USER].fixture(autouse=True) def reimport_component_module(): sys.modules.pop("my_component", None) ``` With this fixture both tests pass. Replacing the component callable with a stub in tests also works. **Suggested fix.** `_mount_component` closes over only `component_key` and `isolate_styles`, but `_create_component_callable()` has the raw `html`, `css` and `js` in scope. If it kept them, `_mount_component` could register the definition into the current registry when the name is missing there, before mounting. File-backed definitions would need their paths resolved against that registry. Alternatively, keep a process-level record of inline definitions and seed each new `AppTest` registry from it. **Related.** #15484 (AppTest did not discover installed CCv2 components) and #14274 (AppTest `TypeError` with CCv2) are both closed. #14274's reproducer used this same imported-module pattern with a single test. The regression test added with its fix (#14301) defines the component inside `AppTest.from_function`, so it registers again on every run and does not cover this case.

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17216)

This is a real `AppTest` isolation bug for inline `st.components.v2` components defined in an imported module. `st.components.v2.component()` registers once at import time into `get_bidi_component_manager()`, which is the active runtime’s `BidiComponentManager` (or a throwaway local manager if no runtime exists). Each `AppTest` instance builds a fresh manager, runs `discover_and_register_components()` (installed packages only), then clears `Runtime._instance` after the run. Python caches the helper module, so later instances never re-call `component()`, and `st._bidi_component` raises `Component '<name>' is not registered.` Looking the name up on the current runtime. Importing the module before the first `AppTest` registers into a discarded manager, so every test fails. Defining the component in the script body still works because it re-registers every run; that is also why `test_v2_custom_component` (added for #14274) does not cover this case.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14274 — Closed. Same imported-module CCv2 + `AppTest` pattern, but a single test that crashed with `TypeError` because the mock runtime had no `bidi_component_registry`. The fix (#14301) still defines the component inside `AppTest.from_function`, so it re-registers every run.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15484 — Closed. Another AppTest vs CCv2 registry gap: AppTest did not discover installed/file-backed components. That path is package discovery; this one is inline definitions that live only in the first instance’s registry.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9139 — Open. Same class of AppTest process-level leak: state from one `AppTest` (`st.cache_data` there, the CCv2 registry here) is visible or missing in a later instance in the same pytest process.
